references.name: Faces
references.summary: Select named planar faces for within-component feature operations.
references.use_when: Pass a Faces value to operations such as Shape.on() and Shape.shell() to identify a surface of the target body.
references.limits: The enum defines all six cardinal faces. Individual operations may support only a subset; Shape.on() currently accepts TOP and BOTTOM. Component assembly attachment uses Anchor instead.

references.name: Anchor
references.summary: Select component attachment references and cardinal directions.
references.use_when: Use cardinal or corner anchors to attach reusable component occurrences, or combine cardinal values to identify Box edges/corners.
references.limits: Anchor is the assembly/alignment vocabulary. Within-component feature placement normally uses Faces instead. INNER_BOTTOM has no direction vector and therefore cannot be used as a cardinal selector.

references.name: Axis
references.summary: Select one of the native principal X, Y or Z axes.
references.use_when: Use Axis for primitive orientation and supported patterns, for example Cylinder(..., axis=Axis.X) or a linear Hole pattern along Axis.Y.
references.limits: Axis is a principal-axis selector, not an attachment reference and not an extrusion Direction.

references.name: Direction
references.summary: Choose how an extrusion extends relative to its sketch-plane normal.
references.use_when: Pass a Direction to Sketch.extrude() when the default positive extrusion is not the intended direction.
references.limits: Direction describes extrusion relative to the sketch plane; it is not a world-axis selector. Use Axis for principal X/Y/Z directions.

references.name: Depth
references.summary: Choose a supported feature-depth policy.
references.use_when: Use Depth.THROUGH_ALL for features such as Hole that should pass completely through their target instead of using a fixed distance.
references.limits: THROUGH_ALL is currently the only named depth policy.

references.name: Edges
references.summary: Select edges for supported fillet and chamfer feature operations.
references.use_when: Use Edges.VERTICAL for the vertical edges of a supported rectangular body. Use from_profile() for named profile segments and from_vertices() for extrusion-axis edges grown from named profile vertices.
references.limits: Only the selectors implemented here are public. from_profile() currently supports sides="both"; from_vertices() requires named Polygon2D vertices.

references.name: Shape
references.summary: Represent Forge geometry/feature intent before SolidCraft executes it.
references.use_when: Shape values are normally returned by constructors such as Box(), Cylinder(), Hole() and Sketch.extrude(), then transformed or combined with the supported Shape methods/operators.
references.limits: Shape is Forge's model-intent node, not a second geometry kernel. SolidCraft owns the final BRep and native feature history; users normally do not instantiate Shape(kind, data) directly.
references.signature: Shape(kind: str, data: Any, history: Any = None) -> None

references.name: component
references.summary: Declare one reusable physical component definition.
references.use_when: Decorate a model class when its build() result represents one reusable physical part. Calling the decorated class creates an occurrence of that shared definition.
references.limits: build() must produce one Shape when the class is reused as a component. Public lower-case numeric fields become editable native parameters; underscore-prefixed inputs remain Forge/build-time inputs.

references.name: assembly
references.summary: Declare a reusable class that composes component occurrences.
references.use_when: Decorate a class when the class itself represents a reusable assembly or subassembly built from component occurrences and their relationships.
references.limits: build() must return a component occurrence or Assembly. The decorator does not itself create grouping or attachment relationships; those come from the objects returned by build().

references.name: Occurrence.copy
references.summary: Create another occurrence of the same reusable definition.
references.use_when: Reuse the same physical component definition at another placement.
references.limits: copy() does not duplicate the component feature definition. The new occurrence starts without the source attachment and explicit name.

references.name: Occurrence.move
references.summary: Translate an occurrence without changing its shared component geometry.
references.use_when: The intended design rule is an explicit placement/offset rather than a relationship to a face, corner or datum of another part.
references.limits: move() clears an existing attachment because it defines placement directly. Parameter/Expression inputs stay symbolic where supported; use attach() when another component should own the relationship.

references.name: Occurrence.attach
references.summary: Create a rigid relationship from this occurrence to another component.
references.use_when: Placement should be expressed semantically between component references, such as left face to right face or one mounting frame to another, rather than as a calculated global XYZ position.
references.limits: The target must be another component occurrence. Supported standard anchors currently focus on rectangular component geometry; custom AnchorFrame/AnchorTopology references cover more specific datums. as_built=True records the existing pose and takes no anchor/offset relationship arguments.
references.signature: Occurrence.attach(self, target, *, parent=<Anchor.RIGHT: 'right'>, child=<Anchor.LEFT: 'left'>, offset=(0, 0), gap=0, angle=None, as_built=False)

references.name: Occurrence.group
references.summary: Place this occurrence in a named native subassembly component.
references.use_when: Give one occurrence a useful native browser/subassembly parent.
references.limits: Grouping changes hierarchy only. It does not align, attach or otherwise create a mechanical relationship. One occurrence cannot belong to several different groups.

references.name: Assembly.group
references.summary: Wrap these assembly occurrences in a real nested native component.
references.use_when: The collection should appear as one named subassembly/browser unit in SolidCraft.
references.limits: Grouping changes native hierarchy, not placement or relationships. Use attach() for mechanical relationships between occurrences.

references.name: Assembly.with_anchor
references.summary: Expose one named attachment datum owned by this assembly.
references.use_when: A mounting/reference name belongs to the meaning of the larger assembly rather than to the generic reusable component itself.
references.limits: target must be an occurrence already in this Assembly. offset is an optional in-plane correction to pass through to attach(); this does not create the attachment by itself.

references.name: Assembly.anchor
references.summary: Return one named assembly-owned attachment datum.
references.use_when: A consumer needs the target/reference pair previously exposed with with_anchor() in order to create an attachment.
references.limits: The name must resolve to exactly one assembly-owned anchor.

references.name: Shape.at
references.summary: Place a shape at absolute coordinates or align it to another Shape.
references.use_when: Use shape.at(x, y, z) for geometric placement. A Box may additionally use a cardinal anchor. Use shape.at(target) for the supported shape-to-shape CENTER alignment.
references.limits: Shape-to-shape alignment currently supports CENTER-to-CENTER only. at() is geometric placement/alignment; selecting a support face for a feature is the job of Shape.on().
references.signature: Shape.at(self, x=0, y=0, z=0, *, anchor=<Anchor.CENTER: 'center'>, child=<Anchor.CENTER: 'center'>)

references.name: Shape.on
references.summary: Place a supported within-component feature on a target face.
references.use_when: Put a Hole or another supported feature on an existing Shape and select its entry/support surface with Faces.
references.limits: Shape.on() currently accepts Faces.TOP and Faces.BOTTOM. This is feature placement; component assembly attachment uses Anchor and the component occurrence attach() API.

references.name: Shape.attach
references.summary: Anchor a supported feature explicitly to another Shape.
references.use_when: Use this lower-level feature-placement form when parent/child Anchor references are required explicitly.
references.limits: This is legacy within-component feature anchoring. Prefer on() for simple face placement. It is separate from component occurrence attachment used by assemblies.

references.name: Shape.shell
references.summary: Hollow a supported solid and leave selected Faces open.
references.use_when: Create an enclosure-like body with an even wall thickness while removing one or more named planar faces.
references.limits: open= must be one Faces value or a non-empty sequence of Faces values. Support still depends on the underlying feature tree.

references.name: Sketch
references.summary: Create an explicit named 2D sketch scope.
references.use_when: Author one or more 2D profiles before creating a 3D extrusion. A Sketch may be standalone on XY/XZ/YZ or supported by an existing Shape.
references.limits: Sketch(on=target) selects the supporting shape; profile placement inside the sketch is a separate operation. Leave the with-scope before extruding.
references.signature: Sketch(*, name='Profile', on=None, parent=<Anchor.TOP: 'top'>, plane=None, origin=None, offset=None)

references.name: Sketch.add
references.summary: Add a supported 2D profile to this Sketch.
references.use_when: Explicitly add or reposition Circle2D, Rectangle2D, Polygon2D, RoundedRectangle2D or Text2D geometry in the active sketch.
references.limits: Placement currently uses numeric offset=(x, y). Semantic 2D anchor placement is not implemented by this method yet.

references.name: Sketch.extrude
references.summary: Extrude a completed Sketch into a supported 3D feature.
references.use_when: Leave the Sketch context and then create material using a finite distance and, when needed, a Direction relative to the sketch plane.
references.limits: A standalone Sketch requires a finite distance. Depth.THROUGH_ALL is only meaningful for a Sketch attached to an existing Shape.

references.name: geometry-constructors
references.summary: Direct 3D primitives and 2D profile constructors.

members.name: Box
members.summary: Create a native rectangular solid.
members.use_when: Model a simple rectangular part directly without introducing a Sketch.
members.limits: The conventional Box base lies in XY and thickness extends along +Z. Use at() for supported placement/anchor semantics.

members.name: Cylinder
members.summary: Create a native cylinder on a principal axis.
members.use_when: Model a cylindrical primitive directly and choose Axis.X, Axis.Y or Axis.Z for its direction.
members.limits: .at(x, y, z) places the cylinder by its base point. axis must be a principal Axis value.

members.name: Sphere
members.summary: Create a sphere from its radius.
members.use_when: A direct spherical primitive is sufficient.
members.limits: Sphere has no separate orientation axis; use Shape placement/CSG operations where supported.

members.name: Rectangle2D
members.summary: Create a rectangular 2D profile.
members.use_when: Author a simple rectangle inside an explicit Sketch before extrusion.
members.limits: The profile is authored in sketch coordinates; use the Sketch to choose its plane and placement.

members.name: RoundedRectangle2D
members.summary: Create a native rounded-rectangle 2D profile.
members.use_when: A sketch needs a rectangle with true circular corner arcs rather than a polygonal approximation.
members.limits: Current support is inside an explicit Sketch. The radius must be below half the shorter side.

members.name: Circle2D
members.summary: Create a circular 2D profile by diameter or radius.
members.use_when: Author a circular profile inside an explicit Sketch.
members.limits: Supply exactly one of d= or r=; the Sketch determines the plane.

members.name: Polygon2D
members.summary: Create a closed named or unnamed polygon profile.
members.use_when: A 2D profile needs arbitrary straight segments or named vertices and segments that later drive selectors such as Edges.from_profile().
members.limits: At least three 2D points are required. plane is XY, XZ or YZ. world=True currently supports only XZ and lets input use intuitive world (x, z) coordinates.

references.name: feature-constructors
references.summary: Manufacturing and plastic-feature intent added to supported bodies.

members.name: Hole
members.summary: Create hole feature intent, optionally directional and countersunk.
members.use_when: Remove a manufacturing-style hole from a supported body. Simple holes can be placed with on(); directional or countersunk holes can use the native Hole path with explicit placement.
members.limits: Diameter must be positive. depth is a positive distance or Depth.THROUGH_ALL. Countersink diameter must exceed the hole diameter.
members.signature: Hole(*, d, depth=<Depth.THROUGH_ALL: 'through_all'>, direction=None, countersink_d=None, countersink_angle=90, countersink_recess=0)

members.name: Lip
members.summary: Create plastic enclosure lip feature intent.
members.use_when: Add a lip to a supported shelled enclosure rim using feature placement.
members.limits: Placement and parent-shape support follow the feature-placement API.

members.name: SnapFit
members.summary: Create cantilever snap-fit feature intent.
members.use_when: Add a plastic snap feature to a supported face with an explicit hook direction.
members.limits: hook must be one 3D direction; optional direction must also be an XYZ triple. Placement uses the supported feature-placement API.
members.signature: SnapFit(*, length, thickness, width, catch_depth, catch_length, hook, direction=None)

members.name: Boss
members.summary: Create plastic screw-boss feature intent.
members.use_when: Add a cylindrical support boss, optionally with a central hole, to a supported face.
members.limits: Optional direction is an XYZ triple. The active History policy can affect how the boss is lowered.

members.name: Rest
members.summary: Create plastic support/rest feature intent.
members.use_when: Add a support pad or elongated rest to a supported face.
members.limits: Optional along and direction values are XYZ triples. Placement uses the supported feature-placement API.
members.signature: Rest(*, width, height, length=None, along=None, direction=None)

references.name: parameters-positioning
references.summary: Keep dimensions symbolic and express readable offsets or parent-bound positions.

members.name: Parameter
members.summary: Represent one named editable CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Keep a value symbolic so generated SolidCraft commands can retain an editable dependency instead of baking in the current Python number.
members.limits: Names must be valid Python identifiers and values finite numbers. Normal public lower-case model fields are usually promoted to parameters automatically, so explicit Parameter() is mainly useful in lower-level or assembly code.

members.name: X
members.summary: Axis token with MIN, CENTER and MAX parent-bound placement selectors.
members.use_when: Public X, Y and Z tokens let feature offsets refer to a parent bound, for example X.MIN + 10 or Y.MAX - 10, without hard-coding the current global coordinate.
members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: Y
members.summary: Axis token with MIN, CENTER and MAX parent-bound placement selectors.
members.use_when: Public X, Y and Z tokens let feature offsets refer to a parent bound, for example X.MIN + 10 or Y.MAX - 10, without hard-coding the current global coordinate.
members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: Z
members.summary: Axis token with MIN, CENTER and MAX parent-bound placement selectors.
members.use_when: Public X, Y and Z tokens let feature offsets refer to a parent bound, for example X.MIN + 10 or Y.MAX - 10, without hard-coding the current global coordinate.
members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: up
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the +Z direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

members.name: down
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the -Z direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

members.name: left
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the -X direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

members.name: right
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the +X direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

members.name: front
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the -Y direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

members.name: back
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the +Y direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

members.name: half
members.summary: Return half of a numeric or symbolic CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Keep midpoint-style arithmetic readable without converting a symbolic CAD dimension to a concrete Python value.
members.limits: Equivalent to value / 2; the input must support that operation.

members.name: midpoint
members.summary: Return the midpoint between two numeric or symbolic dimensions.
members.use_when: Express a centre position while preserving symbolic CAD dependencies.
members.limits: Equivalent to (start + end) / 2; inputs must support symbolic arithmetic.

members.name: pv
members.summary: Return the concrete Python value of a symbolic CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Python itself genuinely needs a number for validation or control flow.
members.limits: Calling pv() intentionally removes the symbolic dependency at that point. Geometry and placement should normally keep Parameter/Expression objects symbolic so SolidCraft remains editable and associative.

references.name: attachment-references
references.summary: Use richer local or topology-backed datums when a standard Anchor is not enough.

members.name: AnchorFrame
members.summary: Describe one local attachment point and orientation.
members.use_when: A standard face or corner Anchor is not enough and the mounting datum needs its own local origin plus orientation. A reusable component may expose named AnchorFrame values from anchors(), or an assembly may pass one directly to attach().
members.limits: origin is component-local. z is the attachment normal and x fixes the clocking around that normal; both directions must be non-zero and not parallel. Direct frames on explicitly rotated occurrences have limited support as documented by the assembly guide.
members.signature: AnchorFrame(origin: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), z: tuple[float, float, float] | scpf.core.Anchor = <Anchor.TOP: 'top'>, x: tuple[float, float, float] | scpf.core.Anchor = <Anchor.RIGHT: 'right'>) -> None

members.name: AnchorTopology
members.summary: Describe an attachment datum that follows native SolidCraft topology.
members.use_when: A relationship should follow a particular edge, adjacent planar face and optionally one endpoint as dimensions change, rather than freezing one XYZ coordinate.
members.limits: edge and on are native selection pick points; corner is optional. z and x may override frame orientation. Current Forge support focuses on planar-face edges and non-rotated occurrences.
members.signature: AnchorTopology(edge: tuple[float, float, float], on: tuple[float, float, float], corner: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, z: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, x: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None) -> None

references.name: history-control
references.summary: Control supported feature-history lowering without changing geometry intent.

members.name: History
members.summary: Choose how supported semantic features are lowered to native history.
members.use_when: Select AUTO for normal Forge behaviour, or deliberately request one of the supported native/sketch history policies inside behavior().
members.limits: This is a compiler-history policy, not a geometry operation. Exact effects depend on the feature being compiled.

members.name: behavior
members.summary: Temporarily select a History policy for objects created in the scope.
members.use_when: A model intentionally needs to compare or request a particular supported lowering strategy without changing the geometry API.
members.limits: The policy applies only inside the context and only to features that inspect the active history setting.

references.name: execution-api
references.summary: Lower-level entry points for compiling Shapes or trusted model source files.

members.name: compile_model
members.summary: Compile one Shape tree to a native SolidCraft command document.
members.use_when: Lower-level tooling already has a final Shape object and needs the JSON command plan without executing a model source file.
members.limits: The final value must be a Shape and name must be a valid identifier. Normal user workflows usually call the scpf runner/CLI instead.

members.name: run_script
members.summary: Execute a trusted SCPF model source file and return its command document.
members.use_when: Programmatic tooling needs the same model-loading/root-selection and compilation behaviour as the SCPF CLI.
members.limits: The source is executed as trusted Python. A file must either end in an explicit root model call or define exactly one unambiguous public model class with build().

references.name: diagnostics
references.summary: Public diagnostics for invalid model intent and lost symbolic parameter dependencies.

members.name: ModelError
members.summary: Report unsupported or invalid CAD model intent.
members.use_when: Catch Forge compilation/model validation failures separately from normal Python argument errors when integrating the lower-level compiler API.
members.limits: User model code normally fixes the underlying model instead of handling this exception as a recoverable geometry result.

members.name: ModelParameterWarning
members.summary: Warn that an editable model parameter lost a native CAD dependency.
members.use_when: Tooling wants to detect parameters that became concrete Python values or are only partly associative in the generated SolidCraft model.
members.limits: This is a warning category, not an exception. The preferred fix is to preserve the symbolic relationship or mark an intentional build-time input with a leading underscore.
